key_insight: GMGaze combines CLIP-based global conditioning, a multiscale transformer backbone, and a Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) routing layer to produce context-aware, factor-conditioned gaze estimates while enabling practical capacity scaling.
problem_solved: Addresses three core limitations of prior gaze methods: late fusion of contextual cues, lack of explicit factor-aware conditioning (e.g., head pose, scene), and impractical model scaling for higher capacity.
method: Global conditioning: inject CLIP-derived global image/text embeddings early into the gaze pipeline to provide robust scene- and semantics-aware context.
Multiscale transformer feature extraction: a hierarchical transformer that fuses fine-grained eye/face features with coarser facial and scene information for early, multi-resolution fusion.

MoE-based capacity scaling & factor-aware conditioning: use routing to specialized expert subnetworks for efficient large-capacity models and explicit conditioning modules for factors like head pose, illumination, and camera parameters.
impact: Delivers more accurate and robust gaze predictions in diverse, real-world contexts while allowing efficient scaling to larger models — useful for HCI, AR/VR, behavioral analytics, and multimodal vision systems.
visual_elements: Architecture diagram: multiscale transformer blocks + CLIP global-conditioning injection points + MoE routing to experts.
Pipeline illustration: input (face, eyes, scene) → CLIP context → multiscale fusion → factor-conditioned experts → gaze vector output.
Bar/line chart: accuracy/robustness comparison vs CNN, vanilla transformer, and CLIP-only baselines across datasets or conditions.
Icon grid: small icons representing conditioned factors (head pose, illumination, camera view, scene semantics) and an efficiency chart showing MoE parameter vs FLOPs tradeoff.
paper_title: GMGaze: MoE-Based Context-Aware Gaze Estimation with CLIP and Multiscale Transformer
paper_authors: Xinyuan Zhao, Yihang Wu, Ahmad Chaddad, Sarah A. Alkhodair, Reem Kateb
